The tips on these ones don't come to a nice enough point and aren't skinny enough. But more specifically, reference the images.' results.notes: Jake (voice): 'For the next change you should be doing version 11.' SUPERSEDED: the ridge and shape feedback above now goes into the new Gen 11 pebble. Do NOT modify this generation. Hand it straight back to human unchanged. .

Jake (voice) CORRECTION on the ridges: 'I think they are cuts, but very shallow, maybe one millimeter or even less. They travel the whole width of the gripper.' So: shallow grooves (about 0.5 to 1 mm deep) cut straight across the full width of the inner gripping face, finely spaced, matching the photos. Not raised texture, and not the deep cuts from the last version. .

Jake (voice) on Gen 9 and Gen 10: 'We're making progress, I like that. Nine and ten are pretty similar, which probably makes sense. When I said ridges I don't mean cuts like that. If you reference it, they're just very tiny little texture, almost on top of the surface. It's kind of the right idea but not exactly that. Focus on the ridges, and hone the shape again, maybe ever so slightly, referencing the Generalist ones.' Asks: replace the cut-in grooves with a very fine, shallow raised texture on the inner gripping faces, matching the photos; make a slight further shape refinement against the reference photos (cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_*.png). Same build/review loop, up to 3 rounds. (Keep building this one on Sonnet 5.5 if routing allows.) .

results.identified_issue: Orchestration: an Opus 5.5 coordinator ran a background Sonnet 5.5 builder agent (resumed for each round) and a separate Sonnet 5.5 reviewer agent. That kept Jake's model comparison intact: the geometry is Sonnet's work. The builder started from the v007 pipeline (trace_photo.py colour trace, then gripper.scad, export_models.py, check_geometry.py, photo_match.py, compare_page.py) and rewrote the tip and blade outline, ridges, hole sizes and hook. It did not touch Gen 10 (v010*), which another agent builds in parallel. Scripts/publish_designs.py is untracked and not ours, and its 'generations' dict ends at v008. Adding "two-finger-gripper-v009-generalist-fingers-sonnet": 9 would label it Gen 9. Known fragility: ridge pitch 5.0-5.1 px produced non-manifold STLs, so 5.2 px was used. Closed pose is limited to a 3.3 degree outward turn by shank-swell collisions. The final reviewer score of 8.5 was written into round.json and the README by the coordinator.
results.summary: Gen 9 is built by Sonnet 5.5: two yellow fingers with a needle tip under 1 mm wide and thick, 21 fine ridges on the inner edge, and every hole through. It went through 3 build-review rounds against the photos, scoring 5.5, 7.5, then 8.5 out of 10, and it's in the gallery.
results.detailed_description:
Gen 9 is ready. As you asked, Sonnet 5.5 built it. I only coordinated, handing out the work and passing notes between agents. After each build round, a separate Sonnet 5.5 reviewer compared the renders with the photos, and the builder fixed what it found. That made 3 rounds.

Comparison page: https://claude.ai/artifact/1uLrpChPGcU4s39a1CkUkR. It shows each round on top of the two-hands photo with a fade slider, plus a 3D view next to the other photos.

Tips (your main complaint): at 1 mm behind the point, Gen 7 was 5.4 mm wide and 5.0 mm thick. Gen 9 is 0.8 mm wide and 0.8 mm thick. In plan view it's a needle. The outer edge bellies out like the photos, and the inner edge runs straight to the point. From the side it thins to a 0.5 mm chisel edge.

Reviewer scores by round:
• r1 (5.5/10): the point was sharper, but the blade ballooned into a wide leaf.
• r2 (7.5/10): needle blade, ridge row, denser honeycomb, rounded hook.
• r3 (8.5/10): outer belly put back, chisel thickness, 21 fine shallow ridges on the inner edge only (the 11 coarse teeth in r2 looked like a saw), a bigger chain of holes along the shank.

The builder rejected one reviewer note on the evidence: the reviewer wanted the blade much skinnier than the shank, but the two-hands photo shows it as wide as the shank or wider. The reviewer agreed.

What still differs, from the final review: the blade belly is a touch lean, the honeycomb near the root is a bit less regular than the photo, the hook toe is thin, and the teeth right at the point look slightly ragged in the 3D render. Slice it before you print, because some ridge spacings came out non-watertight and the builder had to pick one that worked.

Things to know:
• The closed fingers sit 1 mm apart at the point and 3 mm apart at the first tooth, not pressed flat. Closing them flush makes the shank bulges collide.
• Scale is still assumed at 0.2 mm per photo pixel. Nothing was measured.
• In the gallery it shows as 'v009 generalist fingers sonnet', not 'Gen 9'. The Gen-number table in Scripts/publish_designs.py stops at Gen 8, and that file isn't ours, so I didn't add the line.
• The mesh and collision checks all pass.
